summary: npm package ships a fake Cloudflare Turnstile phishing/redirect lure page as its sole content
details: The package contains a single index.html that impersonates a Cloudflare 'Just a moment...' Turnstile challenge page (data-sitekey="0x4AAAAAADrvn4rDM7WVvgPh"). Its onTurnstileComplete handler contains obfuscator.io-style code that decodes a target URL from an encoded string array, appends the current query-string parameters, and invokes window.location.assign() to redirect the visitor. There are no npm lifecycle scripts and main is an HTML file, so installing or require()ing the package does not execute code on the installer's machine. The package's sole purpose is to abuse the npm registry (and its CDN mirrors such as unpkg/jsDelivr) as free hosting infrastructure for a phishing/redirect lure that targets end users who load the page via a CDN URL. The random-looking package name, noindex/nofollow meta tags, and obfuscated redirect logic are consistent with disposable phishing-kit hosting.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
